questions.text_english: Which among the following is a false statement?

options.A: शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया वेग अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता से स्वतंत्र होता है।
options.B: शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया की अर्द्ध-आयु, वेग स्थिरांक के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।
options.C: किसी अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता शून्य हो सकती है।
options.D: प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए t₁/₂ = 0.693/k

options_english.A: Rate of zero order reaction is independent of initial concentration of reactant.
options_english.B: Half-life of a zero order reaction is inversely proportional to the rate constant.
options_english.C: Molecularity of a reaction may be zero.
options_english.D: For a first order reaction, t₁/₂ = 0.693/k.

questions.solution: Option (C) is false because molecularity of a reaction is always a positive integer (1, 2, or 3) and can never be zero or a fraction. Molecularity represents the number of molecules colliding in an elementary step, so zero is physically meaningless. Options (A), (B), and (D) are all true statements about zero-order and first-order reactions.

questions.text: 1 मोल MnO₄⁻ को MnO₂ में अपचयित करने के लिए आवश्यक आवेश है
questions.text_english: The charge required for the reduction of 1 mol of MnO₄⁻ to MnO₂ is
questions.solution: In MnO₄⁻, the oxidation state of Mn is +7. In MnO₂, the oxidation state of Mn is +4. The change in oxidation state is +7 to +4, which means 3 electrons are gained per Mn atom. Therefore, 1 mole of MnO₄⁻ requires 3 moles of electrons, i.e., 3 Faradays (3 F) of charge. Options A, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.text: [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास वाला तत्व है
questions.text_english: The element having [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ electronic configuration is
questions.solution: Copper (Cu, Z=29) has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ due to the extra stability associated with completely filled d-orbitals. Although one might expect [Ar]3d⁹4s², copper adopts [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ for extra stability. Zinc (Zn) has [Ar]3d¹⁰4s², Cr has [Ar]3d⁵4s¹, and Mn has [Ar]3d⁵4s².

questions.text: अणुओं की संख्या जो किसी प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में परस्पर अभिक्रिया करते हैं, एक माप होती है
questions.text_english: The number of molecules that react with each other in an elementary reaction is a measure of the:
questions.solution: Molecularity is defined as the number of reacting species (atoms, ions, or molecules) that must collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction to bring about a chemical reaction. Hence option (C) is correct. Order is determined experimentally from the rate law, stoichiometry refers to molar ratios, and activation energy is the minimum energy barrier for a reaction.

questions.text: प्रतिचुंबकीय स्पीशीज़ है [परमाणु संख्या : Co = 27, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.text_english: The diamagnetic species is: [At. No. Co = 27, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.solution: In [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻, Ni is in +2 state with configuration d⁸. CN⁻ is a strong field ligand causing pairing of electrons, resulting in dsp² hybridization with all electrons paired — hence diamagnetic. In [NiCl₄]²⁻, Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand, so electrons remain unpaired (paramagnetic). [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ has Fe³⁺ (d⁵) with one unpaired electron (paramagnetic). [CoF₆]³⁻ has Co³⁺ with F⁻ as weak field ligand, leaving unpaired electrons. Therefore option (A) is correct.

questions.text: संकुल आयन [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]²⁺ तथा [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]²⁺ कहलाते हैं
questions.text_english: The complex ions [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]²⁺ and [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]²⁺ are called
questions.solution: Linkage isomers arise when a ligand can coordinate to the central metal atom through different donor atoms. The NO₂⁻ ion can bind through nitrogen (–NO₂, nitro) or through oxygen (–ONO, nitrito). Hence [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]²⁺ and [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]²⁺ are linkage isomers. Ionization isomers differ in the ions in solution, coordination isomers involve exchange between inner and outer spheres, and geometrical isomers differ in spatial arrangement.

questions.text: द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉल की क्रोमिक ऐनहाइड्राइड (CrO₃) के साथ ऑक्सीकरण अभिक्रिया के बाद क्या बनेगा?
questions.text_english: What will be formed after oxidation reaction of secondary alcohol with chromic anhydride (CrO₃)?
questions.solution: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol (R–CHOH–R') with CrO₃ yields a ketone (R–CO–R'). Secondary alcohols have the –OH group on a carbon that also carries two other carbon groups; oxidation removes two hydrogen atoms to form the C=O of a ketone. Primary alcohols give aldehydes (and further to carboxylic acids), while secondary alcohols cannot be oxidized beyond ketones under mild conditions. Hence option (B) is correct.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कौन सा सही IUPAC नाम है? (बेंज़ीन वलय पर CH₃ और Cl para स्थिति में)
questions.text_english: Which is the correct IUPAC name for the compound shown (benzene ring with CH₃ at top and Cl at bottom in para positions)?
questions.solution: As per IUPAC rules, when two substituents are present on a benzene ring, the one that comes first alphabetically in the name receives the lower locant. However, the correct IUPAC name gives the principal characteristic group or the substituent with higher seniority the lower number. In this case the compound is 1-methyl-4-chlorobenzene (also acceptable as 4-chlorotoluene using retained name). Option (D) 1-Methyl-4-Chlorobenzene correctly names CH₃ at C1 and Cl at C4. Option (C) reverses the numbering without proper justification. Toluene (B) has no Cl. Option (A) is not a proper IUPAC name.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा/से प्रोटीन के विकृतीकरण का उदाहरण है/हैं?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is/are examples of denaturation of protein?
questions.solution: Denaturation of proteins involves the disruption of the secondary and tertiary structure while the primary structure (peptide bonds) remains intact. Coagulation of egg white on heating and curdling of milk (by acid) are classic examples of protein denaturation. Clotting of blood (option C) involves a complex biochemical cascade and is not primarily a denaturation process. Therefore both (A) and (B) are correct, making option (D) the right answer.

questions.text: फीनॉल का सैलिसिलिक अम्ल में रूपांतरण निम्न में से किसके द्वारा किया जा सकता है?
questions.text_english: The conversion of phenol to salicylic acid can be accomplished by
questions.solution: Kolbe's reaction involves treating sodium phenoxide with CO₂ under pressure at 400 K, followed by acidification, to yield salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). The Reimer-Tiemann reaction converts phenol to o-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde), not salicylic acid. Friedel-Crafts introduces alkyl or acyl groups, and coupling reaction joins diazonium salts with phenols. Therefore option (C) is correct.

questions.text: स्कर्वी रोग किसकी कमी के कारण होता है?
questions.text_english: Scurvy is caused due to deficiency of
questions.solution: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of Vitamin C, which is chemically known as ascorbic acid. It is a water-soluble vitamin essential for collagen synthesis; its deficiency leads to bleeding gums, weakening of blood vessels, and bruising. Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency causes beriberi, Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency causes ariboflavinosis, and glutamic acid is a non-essential amino acid unrelated to scurvy. Hence option (C) is correct.

questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइड आपस में किस बंध द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं?
questions.text_english: Nucleotides are joined together by
questions.solution: In nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), individual nucleotides are covalently linked to each other through phosphodiester bonds. These bonds form between the 3'-OH of one nucleotide's sugar and the phosphate group attached to the 5'-carbon of the next nucleotide. Glycosidic linkage connects the sugar to the nitrogenous base within a nucleoside, peptide bonds link amino acids, and hydrogen bonds hold the two strands of DNA together. Hence option (D) is correct.

Because Cu cannot reduce H⁺ ions to H₂, it does not react with dilute mineral acids to liberate hydrogen gas. Hence option (A) is correct.

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis involves alkylation of the phthalimide anion with an alkyl halide via nucleophilic substitution (SN2), followed by hydrolysis. Aryl halides (C–X bond on benzene ring) are resistant to nucleophilic substitution under normal conditions due to partial double bond character of the C–X bond (resonance) and the sp² character of the carbon. Therefore, aromatic primary amines cannot be synthesized by this method, and the reason given is correct. Hence option (A) is the answer.

questions.text: IUPAC मानदंड के अनुसार निम्नलिखित उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के नाम बताइए : (a) [Co(NH₃)₄(H₂O)Cl]Cl₂  (b) [CrCl₂(en)₂]Cl
questions.text_english: Name the following coordination compounds according to IUPAC norms: (a) [Co(NH₃)₄(H₂O)Cl]Cl₂  (b) [CrCl₂(en)₂]Cl

key_points: (a) Tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride
(b) Dichlorobis(ethylenediamine)chromium(III) chloride

questions.solution:
(a) [Co(NH₃)₄(H₂O)Cl]Cl₂: The central metal is Co. Ligands inside the coordination sphere are 4 NH₃ (tetraammine), 1 H₂O (aqua), and 1 Cl⁻ (chlorido). Co oxidation state: let it be x; charge = x + 0 + 0 – 1 = +2 total inside sphere, and outside are 2 Cl⁻, giving overall neutral. So Co is +3. IUPAC name: Tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride.

(b) [CrCl₂(en)₂]Cl: The central metal is Cr. Ligands are 2 Cl⁻ (dichloro) and 2 en (ethylenediamine, a bidentate ligand — bis(ethylenediamine)). Outside is 1 Cl⁻. Cr oxidation state: x – 2 = +2 inside, overall charge of cation = +1, and 1 Cl⁻ outside. So x = +3. IUPAC name: Dichlorobis(ethylenediamine)chromium(III) chloride.

questions.text: किसी अभिक्रिया के वेग नियम और वेग स्थिरांक से क्या अभिप्राय है? किसी अभिक्रिया की कोटि पहचानें यदि उसके वेग स्थिरांक की इकाइयाँ निम्न हैं: (a) s⁻¹  (b) mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹
questions.text_english: What is meant by the Rate law and Rate constant of a reaction. Identify the order of a reaction if the units of its Rate constant are: (a) s⁻¹  (b) mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹

key_points: Rate law: the expression that relates the rate of a reaction to the concentration of reactants raised to their respective powers determined experimentally.
Rate constant (k): the proportionality constant in the rate law expression; its value depends only on temperature.
(a) s⁻¹ corresponds to first order reaction
(b) mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹ corresponds to second order reaction

questions.solution:
Rate law is the experimentally determined expression that relates the rate of a chemical reaction to the concentration of the reactants: Rate = k[A]^m[B]^n, where m and n are determined by experiment, not from stoichiometry. The rate constant (k) is the proportionality constant in this expression; it is independent of concentration but depends on temperature.

For identifying order from units of k: the general unit of k is mol^(1-n) L^(n-1) s⁻¹, where n is the order.
(a) For k with units s⁻¹: 1 – n = 0, so n = 1 → first order reaction.
(b) For k with units mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹: 1 – n = –1, so n = 2 → second order reaction.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित रासायनिक समीकरण को पूर्ण एवं संतुलित कीजिए: (a) 8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O →  (b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ →
questions.text_english: Complete and balance the following chemical equations: (a) 8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O →  (b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ →

key_points: (a) 8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O → 8MnO₂ + 6SO₄²⁻ + 2OH⁻
(b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3Sn⁴⁺ + 7H₂O

questions.solution:
(a) In this reaction, MnO₄⁻ (Mn in +7) is reduced to MnO₂ (Mn in +4), a gain of 3 electrons per Mn. S₂O₃²⁻ (S in +2 average) is oxidized to SO₄²⁻ (S in +6), a loss of 8 electrons per S₂O₃²⁻ unit (4 per S × 2 S). Balancing electrons: 8 × 3 = 24 (gain) and 3 × 8 = 24 (loss). The balanced equation is:
8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O → 8MnO₂ + 6SO₄²⁻ + 2OH⁻

(b) In this reaction, Cr₂O₇²⁻ (Cr in +6) is reduced to Cr³⁺ (gain of 3e⁻ per Cr, 6e⁻ per Cr₂O₇²⁻). Sn²⁺ is oxidized to Sn⁴⁺ (loss of 2e⁻ per Sn). Balancing: 6e⁻ gained = 3 × 2e⁻ lost. The balanced equation is:
Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3Sn⁴⁺ + 7H₂O

(B) प्लैटिनम सतह पर NH₃ का अपघटन शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया है। यदि k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ हो तो N₂ और H₂ के उत्पादन की दरें क्या हैं?
questions.text_english:
(A) The rate constant for a zero order reaction A → P is 0.0030 mol L⁻¹s⁻¹. How long will it take for the initial concentration of A to fall from 0.10 M to 0.075 M?
OR
(B) The decomposition of NH₃ on platinum surface is zero order reaction. What are the rates of production of N₂ and H₂ if k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹?

key_points: (B) 2NH₃ → N₂ + 3H₂; Rate of reaction = k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹; Rate of N₂ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ / 2 × 1 = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹; Rate of H₂ = 3 × 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ = 3.75 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹

questions.solution:
(A) For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate law is: [A]t = [A]₀ – kt. Rearranging: t = ([A]₀ – [A]t) / k = (0.10 – 0.075) / 0.0030 = 0.025 / 0.0030 = 8.33 seconds. It will take approximately 8.33 seconds for the concentration to fall from 0.10 M to 0.075 M.

(B) The decomposition reaction is: 2NH₃ → N₂ + 3H₂. The overall rate of reaction = k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. Rate of production of N₂ = (1/2) × k × 2 ... using stoichiometry: d[N₂]/dt = k/2 = (2.5 × 10⁻⁴)/2 = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. Rate of production of H₂ = (3/2) × k = 3 × 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ = 3.75 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित प्रेक्षणों के लिए कारण दीजिए: (a) 443 K पर p-क्लोरोनाइट्रोबेन्जीन, जलीय NaOH के साथ अभिक्रिया करके p-नाइट्रोफीनॉल देता है जबकि क्लोरोबेन्जीन उसी अभिक्रयक के साथ 623 K और 300 atm पर अभिक्रिया करता है। (b) जब क्लोरोएथेन, KCN के साथ अभिक्रिया करता है तब मुख्य उत्पाद प्रोपेन नाइट्राइल बनता है जबकि AgCN के साथ यह एथिलआइसोसायनाइड बनाता है।
questions.text_english: Give reasons for the following observations: (a) p-Chloronitrobenzene reacts with (aq)NaOH at 443 K to give p-nitrophenol whereas chlorobenzene reacts with the same reagent at 623 K and 300 atm. (b) Main product obtained when chloroethane reacts with KCN is propane nitrile while with AgCN it is ethyl isocyanide.

key_points: (a) The -NO₂ group is electron-withdrawing, which activates the ring toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution at lower temperature and pressure.
(b) KCN is predominantly ionic; the nucleophilic carbon attacks to give nitrile. AgCN is covalent, nitrogen being the nucleophile gives isocyanide.

questions.solution:
(a) In p-chloronitrobenzene, the nitro group (–NO₂) is strongly electron-withdrawing and is present para to the –Cl group. It withdraws electron density from the ring through resonance, making the ring carbon bearing –Cl more electrophilic. This activates the C–Cl bond towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr), allowing the reaction to proceed at 443 K. In chlorobenzene, there is no activating group for SNAr; the C–Cl bond is stronger due to partial double-bond character (resonance), requiring more drastic conditions (623 K, 300 atm) for the reaction to occur.

(b) KCN is a predominantly ionic compound in which CN⁻ acts as an ambident nucleophile. However, carbon is the softer and more polarizable end of CN⁻, and it preferentially attacks the electrophilic carbon of chloroethane via SN2, giving propane nitrile (CH₃CH₂CN) as the main product. AgCN is predominantly covalent with the silver bonded to nitrogen, making nitrogen the attacking end. So the reaction with AgCN gives ethyl isocyanide (CH₃CH₂NC) as the main product.
questions.topic: Nucleophilic Substitution in Haloarenes; Ambident Nucleophiles

questions.text: 298 K पर जल में CO₂ के लिए हेनरी नियम का स्थिरांक 1.67 × 10⁸ Pa है। समान ताप पर 3.34 × 10⁵ Pa के अंतर्गत बंद किए गए 540 g सोडा जल में CO₂ के मोलों की संख्या की गणना कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Henry's law constant for CO₂ in water is 1.67 × 10⁸ Pa at 298 K. Calculate the number of moles of CO₂ in 540 g of soda water when packed under 3.34 × 10⁵ Pa at the same temperature.

key_points: Using Henry's law: p = KH × x; mole fraction x = p / KH = 3.34 × 10⁵ / 1.67 × 10⁸ = 2 × 10⁻³
Moles of water = 540/18 = 30 mol
x(CO₂) = n(CO₂) / (n(CO₂) + 30) ≈ n(CO₂) / 30 (since n is very small)

questions.solution:
According to Henry's law, p = KH × x, where p is the partial pressure of the gas, KH is Henry's law constant, and x is the mole fraction of the gas in solution.

Given: KH = 1.67 × 10⁸ Pa, p = 3.34 × 10⁵ Pa
Mole fraction of CO₂: x(CO₂) = p / KH = (3.34 × 10⁵) / (1.67 × 10⁸) = 2 × 10⁻³

Moles of water in 540 g: n(H₂O) = 540 / 18 = 30 mol

Since x(CO₂) is very small: x(CO₂) ≈ n(CO₂) / n(H₂O)
So, n(CO₂) = x(CO₂) × n(H₂O) = 2 × 10⁻³ × 30 = 0.06 mol

The number of moles of CO₂ in 540 g of soda water is 0.06 mol.

questions.text: कारण दीजिए: (a) विद्युत् ऊर्जा उत्पादन के लिए ऊष्मीय संयंत्रों की अपेक्षा ईंधन सेलों को वरीयता दी जाती है। (b) गैल्वेनीकृत पाइप में ज़िंक की परत खंडित होने के उपरान्त भी लोहे में जंग नहीं लगती। (c) वैद्युत-अपघटनी चालकत्व के प्रायोगिक निर्धारण में दिष्टधारा (DC) प्रयुक्त नहीं की जाती है।
questions.text_english: Give reasons: (a) Fuel cells are preferred for production of electrical energy than thermal plants. (b) Iron does not rust even if zinc coating is broken in a galvanized pipe. (c) In the experimental determination of electrolytic conductance, Direct Current (DC) is not used.

key_points: (a) Fuel cells convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy with higher efficiency and no pollution.
(b) Zinc is more reactive; it acts as a sacrificial anode protecting iron even if the coating breaks.
(c) DC causes electrolysis/polarization of electrodes, altering the solution composition and giving erroneous readings.

questions.solution:
(a) Fuel cells convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy through electrochemical reactions, without the intermediate step of burning fuel to produce heat and then converting heat to electricity. This makes them far more efficient (up to ~70%) compared to thermal plants (~40%). They also produce little to no pollution, making them environmentally preferable.

(b) Zinc has a more negative electrode potential than iron (E°Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V; E°Fe²⁺/Fe = –0.44 V). Even if the zinc coating breaks, zinc acts as a sacrificial anode — it preferentially undergoes oxidation and gets corroded while protecting the iron from rusting. This is cathodic protection.

(c) When direct current is used, it causes electrolysis of the solution: ions are discharged at the electrodes and gases may evolve. This changes the composition of the solution and causes polarization of electrodes, leading to back-EMF and inaccurate conductance measurements. Therefore, alternating current (AC) of high frequency is used instead to avoid electrolysis.

questions.text: (a) E°(Mn²⁺/Mn) का मान –1.18 V है। समीपस्थ d-ब्लॉक तत्वों की तुलना में यह मान अत्यन्त ऋणात्मक क्यों है? (b) लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन क्या है? (c) Zn, Cd और Hg कोमल धातुएँ हैं, क्यों?
questions.text_english: (a) E°(Mn²⁺/Mn) is –1.18 V. Why is this value highly negative in comparison to neighbouring d-block elements? (b) What is lanthanoid contraction? (c) Zn, Cd and Hg are soft metals. Why?

key_points: (a) Mn²⁺ has a stable half-filled d⁵ configuration; extra stability means more energy is needed to form Mn²⁺, making E° more negative.
(b) Lanthanoid contraction: the steady decrease in atomic/ionic radii of lanthanoids from La to Lu due to poor shielding by 4f electrons.
(c) Zn, Cd, Hg have completely filled d and s orbitals; no unpaired d electrons means weak metallic bonding, resulting in softness.

questions.solution:
(a) Mn has the configuration [Ar]3d⁵4s². When Mn is oxidized to Mn²⁺, it attains the configuration [Ar]3d⁵, which is an extra stable half-filled d-subshell. This extra stability of Mn²⁺ means that more energy is required to form it from Mn metal; equivalently, the Mn²⁺ ion has little tendency to be reduced back to Mn. This is why the E° value is more negative than that of its neighbouring elements like Cr and Fe.

(b) Lanthanoid contraction is the steady and gradual decrease in the atomic and ionic radii of the lanthanoid elements (La to Lu) with increasing atomic number. This occurs because 4f orbitals have poor shielding ability; as the nuclear charge increases by one unit across the series, the effective nuclear charge experienced by outer electrons increases, pulling electron clouds inward and reducing the size.

(c) Zinc (Zn), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg) have completely filled d¹⁰ and s² outer orbitals with no unpaired d-electrons. The absence of unpaired d-electrons means there is no possibility of d-d metallic bonding, and only weak van der Waals-type forces hold the metal atoms together. This results in low melting points and softness compared to other transition metals.
questions.topic: Properties of d-Block Elements; Lanthanoid Contraction

questions.text: (a) संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धान्त का उपयोग करते हुए, निम्नलिखित के संकरणीकरण और चुंबकीय व्यवहार को समझाइए: (i) [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃  (ii) K₂[NiCl₄]  [परमाणु संख्या : Co = 27, Ni = 28]  (b) d⁵ आयन का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए जब Δ₀ > P है।
questions.text_english: (a) Using valence bond theory, explain the hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the following: (i) [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃  (ii) K₂[NiCl₄]  [At. No. : Co = 27, Ni = 28]  (b) Write the electronic configuration of d⁵ ion when Δ₀ > P.

key_points: (i) Co³⁺ is d⁶; NH₃ is strong field, inner orbital complex, d²sp³ hybridization, diamagnetic
(ii) Ni²⁺ is d⁸; Cl⁻ is weak field, outer orbital complex, sp³ hybridization, paramagnetic (2 unpaired e⁻)
(b) When Δ₀ > P (strong field), d⁵ configuration: t₂g⁵ eg⁰ — one unpaired electron

questions.solution:
(a)(i) [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃: Co is in +3 oxidation state. Co³⁺ has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d⁶. NH₃ is a strong field ligand; it causes pairing of the 3d electrons. The 6 pairs of electrons from NH₃ occupy the d²sp³ hybrid orbitals (2 inner 3d + 1 4s + 3 4p). All 6 d⁶ electrons are paired in three 3d orbitals. Hybridization: d²sp³ (inner orbital complex). Since no unpaired electrons remain, the complex is diamagnetic.

(a)(ii) K₂[NiCl₄]: Ni is in +2 oxidation state. Ni²⁺ has the configuration [Ar]3d⁸. Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand and does not cause pairing. The 4 ligands use sp³ hybrid orbitals of Ni (outer orbital complex). With d⁸ configuration and no pairing forced by Cl⁻, there are 2 unpaired electrons. Hybridization: sp³ (outer orbital). The complex is paramagnetic with 2 unpaired electrons.

(b) When Δ₀ > P (strong field ligand), the d electrons preferentially fill the lower energy t₂g orbitals before occupying the eg orbitals. For a d⁵ ion in a strong field octahedral complex: the configuration is t₂g⁵ eg⁰. This means 5 electrons are in t₂g (with one orbital having 1 electron, two orbitals with 2 electrons each = 2+2+1), giving 1 unpaired electron.
questions.topic: Valence Bond Theory; Crystal Field Theory

questions.text: (a) निम्नलिखित को परिभाषित कीजिए: (i) प्रतिबिंब रूप (एनेंटियोमर)  (ii) रेसिमिक मिश्रण  (b) क्लोरोबेंज़ीन नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति प्रतिरोधी क्यों है?
questions.text_english: (a) Define the following: (i) Enantiomers  (ii) Racemic mixture  (b) Why is chlorobenzene resistant to nucleophilic substitution reaction?

key_points: (i) Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror images of a chiral molecule that differ in rotation of plane-polarized light
(ii) Racemic mixture: equimolar mixture of two enantiomers showing no optical activity
(b) C–Cl bond has partial double bond character due to resonance; C is sp² hybridized; Cl lone pairs donated to ring making C–Cl stronger

questions.solution:
(a)(i) Enantiomers are a pair of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. They contain at least one chiral centre (asymmetric carbon), and each enantiomer rotates plane-polarized light in opposite directions by equal angles — one is dextrorotatory (+) and the other is levorotatory (–). For example, D-lactic acid and L-lactic acid are enantiomers.

(a)(ii) A racemic mixture (or racemate) is an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers of a chiral compound. Because the two enantiomers rotate plane-polarized light in equal but opposite directions, the net optical rotation is zero. A racemic mixture is therefore optically inactive. It is denoted as (±) or dl.

(b) Chlorobenzene is resistant to nucleophilic substitution because: (1) The lone pairs on the Cl atom are in conjugation with the π electrons of the benzene ring, giving the C–Cl bond partial double-bond character. This makes the C–Cl bond shorter and stronger than in chloroalkanes. (2) The carbon of C–Cl is sp² hybridized (planar), and the electron cloud above and below prevents easy approach of a nucleophile. (3) Due to resonance, the electron density on the ring is increased, further repelling the incoming nucleophile. For these reasons, nucleophilic substitution of chlorobenzene requires very harsh conditions.

questions.text:
(A) निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं की व्याख्या कीजिए और सम्मिलित समीकरण लिखिए: (a) वोल्फ-किश्नर अपचयन  (b) एटार्ड अभिक्रिया  (c) कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया
अथवा
(B) निम्न अभिक्रियाओं के अनुक्रम में A, B और C की संरचनाएँ लिखिए: (a) CH₃COOH → (SOCl₂) A → (H₂, Pd-BaSO₄) B → (H₂N–NH₂) C  (b) CH₃CN → (1. DIBAL-H / 2. H₂O) A → (तनु NaOH) B → (Δ) C
questions.text_english:
(A) Explain the following reactions and write chemical equation involved: (a) Wolff-Kishner reduction  (b) Etard reaction  (c) Cannizzaro reaction
OR
(B) Write the structures of A, B and C in the following sequence of reactions: (a) CH₃COOH →(SOCl₂) A →(H₂, Pd-BaSO₄) B →(H₂N–NH₂) C  (b) CH₃CN →(1.DIBAL-H / 2.H₂O) A →(Dil. NaOH) B →(Δ) C

key_points: (A)(a) Wolff-Kishner: aldehyde/ketone + H₂N-NH₂ in KOH/ethylene glycol → alkane + N₂
(A)(b) Etard: toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ → chromium complex → hydrolysis → benzaldehyde
(A)(c) Cannizzaro: HCHO + NaOH → CH₃OH + HCOONa (disproportionation of non-enolizable aldehyde)
(B)(a) A = CH₃COCl, B = CH₃CHO, C = CH₃CH=N-NH₂ (or the hydrazone)
(B)(b) A = CH₃CHO, B = aldol product, C = crotonaldehyde (after dehydration)

questions.solution:
(A)(a) Wolff-Kishner Reduction: An aldehyde or ketone is treated with hydrazine (H₂N-NH₂) in the presence of a base (KOH) and a high boiling solvent (like ethylene glycol) at elevated temperature. The carbonyl group is converted to a –CH₂– group (or –CH₃ for aldehyde) with the release of nitrogen gas. Equation: R–CO–R' + H₂N–NH₂ (KOH/Δ) → R–CH₂–R' + N₂.

(A)(b) Etard Reaction: Toluene (or other methyl-substituted aromatic compound) is treated with chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) in carbon disulfide to form a brown chromium complex. On hydrolysis with water, this complex gives benzaldehyde. Equation: C₆H₅–CH₃ + CrO₂Cl₂ → [Complex] → (H₂O) C₆H₅–CHO.

(A)(c) Cannizzaro Reaction: Aldehydes that have no α-hydrogen atom (non-enolizable), such as formaldehyde (HCHO) or benzaldehyde, undergo a disproportionation reaction in the presence of concentrated NaOH. One molecule is oxidized to carboxylic acid (or its salt) and another is reduced to alcohol. Equation: 2HCHO + NaOH → CH₃OH + HCOONa.

(B)(a) CH₃COOH →(SOCl₂) A (= CH₃COCl, acetyl chloride) →(H₂/Pd-BaSO₄, Rosenmund reduction) B (= CH₃CHO, acetaldehyde) →(H₂N–NH₂) C (= CH₃CH=N–NH₂, acetaldehyde hydrazone).

(B)(b) CH₃CN →(1.DIBAL-H / 2. H₂O) A (= CH₃CHO, acetaldehyde — DIBAL-H reduces nitrile to aldehyde at –78°C) →(Dil. NaOH, aldol condensation) B (= CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO, 3-hydroxybutanal) →(Δ) C (= CH₃CH=CH–CHO, but-2-enal/crotonaldehyde, by dehydration of aldol product).

questions.text: निम्नलिखित शब्दों को परिभाषित कीजिए: (a) प्राकृत प्रोटीन  (b) न्यूक्लियोटाइड  (c) आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल
questions.text_english: Define the following terms: (a) Native protein  (b) Nucleotide  (c) Essential amino acid

key_points: (a) Native protein: a protein in its natural, biologically active, fully folded three-dimensional conformation
(b) Nucleotide: a monomer of nucleic acids consisting of a pentose sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base
(c) Essential amino acid: an amino acid that cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained from the diet

questions.solution:
(a) Native Protein: A native protein is a protein that exists in its natural, biologically active three-dimensional conformation (shape) as found in living cells. It has a specific secondary, tertiary, and (if applicable) quaternary structure stabilized by various bonds and interactions such as hydrogen bonds, disulfide bridges, ionic interactions, and hydrophobic forces. Any disruption of this structure (denaturation) leads to loss of biological activity.

(b) Nucleotide: A nucleotide is the basic structural unit (monomer) of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA). It consists of three components joined together: (1) a five-carbon sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), (2) a phosphate group attached to the 5' carbon of the sugar, and (3) a nitrogenous base (purine — adenine or guanine, or pyrimidine — cytosine, thymine in DNA, or uracil in RNA) attached to the 1' carbon of the sugar. Nucleotides are also important in energy metabolism (e.g., ATP).

(c) Essential Amino Acid: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesized by the human body in sufficient quantities and therefore must be obtained through the diet. There are nine essential amino acids: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine. Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized by the body from other compounds.

questions.text: शुद्ध विलायक से विलयन में अथवा तनु विलयन से सांद्र विलयन में अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली के माध्यम से विलायक का स्वतः प्रवर्तित प्रवाह परासरण कहलाता है। परासरण परिघटना को एक ही आकार के दो अंडों को लेकर प्रदर्शित किया जा सकता है। अंडे में खोल के नीचे और अंडे के पदार्थ के चारों ओर की झिल्ली अर्धपारगम्य होती है। अंडे को तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल में डालकर बाहरी कठोर खोल को हटाया जा सकता है। कठोर खोल को हटाने के बाद एक अंडे को आसुत जल में और दूसरे को संतृप्त नमक के घोल में रखा जाता है। कुछ समय बाद, आसुत जल में रखा अंडा फूल जाता है, जबकि नमक के घोल में रखा अंडा सिकुड़ जाता है। परासरण को रोकने के लिए लगाया गया बाह्य दाब, परासरण दाब (एक अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म) कहलाता है। प्रतिलोम परासरण तब होता है जब लगाया गया बाह्य दाब परासरण दाब से अधिक हो जाता है।
questions.text_english: The spontaneous flow of the solvent through a semipermeable membrane from a pure solvent to a solution or from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution is called osmosis. The phenomenon of osmosis can be demonstrated by taking two eggs of the same size. In an egg, the membrane below the shell and around the egg material is semipermeable. The outer hard shell can be removed by putting the egg in dilute hydrochloric acid. After removing the hard shell, one egg is placed in distilled water and the other in a saturated salt solution. After some time, the egg placed in distilled water swells-up while the egg placed in salt solution shrinks. The external pressure applied to stop the osmosis is termed as osmotic pressure (a colligative property). Reverse osmosis takes place when the applied external pressure becomes larger than the osmotic pressure.

sub_questions.text: प्रतिलोम परासरण को परिभाषित कीजिए। एक अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली (SPM) का नाम बताइए जिसका उपयोग प्रतिलोम परासरण की प्रक्रिया में किया जा सकता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Define reverse osmosis. Name one SPM which can be used in the process of reverse osmosis.

key_points: Reverse osmosis: flow of solvent from solution to pure solvent when applied pressure exceeds osmotic pressure
SPM example: Cellulose acetate membrane

sub_questions.solution: Reverse osmosis is the process in which the solvent flows from the solution (higher solute concentration) to the pure solvent (or lower concentration) through a semipermeable membrane when the external applied pressure exceeds the osmotic pressure of the solution. It is the reverse of normal osmosis and is used commercially for the purification and desalination of seawater. One commonly used semipermeable membrane (SPM) in reverse osmosis is the cellulose acetate membrane.

(i) जब लाल रुधिर कोशिकाओं (RBC) को 0.5% NaCl विलयन में रखा जाता है तो आप क्या होने की अपेक्षा करते हैं?

(ii) 1 M KCl अथवा 1 M यूरिया विलयन में से किसका परासरण दाब अधिक होगा। अपने उत्तर का औचित्य दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) What do you expect to happen when red blood corpuscles (RBC's) are placed in 0.5% NaCl solution?
OR
(ii) Which one of the following will have higher osmotic pressure in 1 M KCl or 1 M urea solution. Justify your answer.

key_points: (i) 0.5% NaCl is hypotonic to blood; RBCs will swell and may burst (hemolysis)
(ii) 1 M KCl dissociates into K⁺ and Cl⁻ giving effective concentration of ~2 M particles; higher osmotic pressure than 1 M urea (non-electrolyte)

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Blood plasma is approximately isotonic with 0.9% NaCl (normal saline). A 0.5% NaCl solution is hypotonic relative to the interior of the RBC. When RBCs are placed in this hypotonic solution, water flows into the cells by osmosis (from region of lower solute concentration to higher). The RBCs will swell up and may eventually burst — a phenomenon called haemolysis.

(ii) 1 M KCl will have higher osmotic pressure. KCl is a strong electrolyte and dissociates completely: KCl → K⁺ + Cl⁻, giving an effective particle concentration of approximately 2 M (i = 2). Urea is a non-electrolyte and does not dissociate, so its effective concentration remains 1 M (i = 1). Since osmotic pressure π = iCRT, the 1 M KCl solution has twice the osmotic pressure of 1 M urea solution.

sub_questions.text: परासरण दाब एक अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म क्यों है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why osmotic pressure is a colligative property?

key_points: Osmotic pressure depends on the number of solute particles (molar concentration), not on the nature/identity of the solute

sub_questions.solution: Osmotic pressure is a colligative property because it depends only on the number (molar concentration) of solute particles dissolved in a given volume of solution, and not on the nature or identity of the solute. The equation π = CRT = (n/V)RT shows that osmotic pressure (π) is directly proportional to the molar concentration (C) of solute, which reflects the number of particles. Two solutions with the same molar concentration of different non-electrolyte solutes will have the same osmotic pressure, confirming its colligative nature.

questions.text: ऐमीनों में नाइट्रोजन परमाणु पर एकाकी इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म होता है जिसके कारण वे लुईस क्षारक की तरह व्यवहार करते हैं। Kb का मान जितना अधिक होगा या pKb का मान जितना कम होगा, क्षारक उतना ही प्रबल होगा। ऐल्कोहॉल, ईथर, एस्टर आदि की तुलना में ऐमीन अधिक क्षारकीय हैं। ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन का क्षारकीय गुण ऐल्किल प्रतिस्थापन की वृद्धि के साथ-साथ बढ़ना चाहिए। लेकिन यह नियमित रूप से नहीं होता है क्योंकि द्वितीयक ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन अप्रत्याशित रूप से जलीय विलयन में तृतीयक ऐमीन की तुलना में अधिक क्षारकीय होता है। ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया और ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन की तुलना में दुर्बल क्षारक होते हैं। इलेक्ट्रॉन मुक्त करने वाले समूह जैसे – CH₃, –OCH₃, –NH₂ आदि, क्षारकीयता को बढ़ाते हैं जबकि इलेक्ट्रॉन खींचने (अपनयन) वाले प्रतिस्थापित समूह जैसे – NO₂, –CN, हैलोजन आदि, ऐमीन की क्षारकीयता को कम करते हैं। इन प्रतिस्थापनों का प्रभाव m– स्थितियों की तुलना में p– पर अधिक होता है।
questions.text_english: Amines have a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom due to which they behave as Lewis base. Greater the value of Kb or smaller the value of pKb, stronger is the base. Amines are more basic than alcohols, ethers, esters, etc. The basic character of aliphatic amines should increase with the increase of alkyl substitution. But it does not occur in a regular manner as a secondary aliphatic amine is unexpectedly more basic than a tertiary amine in aqueous solutions. Aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia and aliphatic amines. Electron releasing groups such as –CH₃, –OCH₃, –NH₂, etc., increase the basicity while electron-withdrawing substituents such as –NO₂, –CN, halogens etc., decrease the basicity of amines. The effect of these substituents is more at p– than at m– position.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित को उनके क्षारकीय गुणों के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए। कारण दीजिए। (aniline, 4-nitro-2-nitroaniline (2,4-dinitroaniline), 4-methylaniline)
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic character. Give reason: aniline, 2,4-dinitroaniline, 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine)

key_points: 2,4-dinitroaniline < aniline < 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine)
–NO₂ groups withdraw electrons decreasing basicity; –CH₃ donates electrons increasing basicity

sub_questions.solution:
The increasing order of basic character is: 2,4-dinitroaniline < aniline < 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine).

Reasoning: In aniline, the lone pair on N is delocalized into the benzene ring, making it a weak base. In 4-methylaniline, the –CH₃ group at the para position is an electron-donating group that increases electron density on the ring and on the nitrogen through inductive and hyperconjugative effects, thereby increasing the availability of the lone pair on N and making it more basic than aniline. In 2,4-dinitroaniline, two strongly electron-withdrawing –NO₂ groups further withdraw electron density from nitrogen by resonance (especially from para and ortho positions), drastically reducing the lone pair availability on N and making it the weakest base of the three.

sub_questions.text: मेथिलऐमीन की तुलना में ऐनिलीन का pKb मान अधिक क्यों होता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why pKb of aniline is more than that of methylamine?

key_points: In aniline, the lone pair on N is delocalized into the benzene ring making it less available for protonation, hence weaker base and higher pKb

sub_questions.solution: The pKb of aniline is higher than that of methylamine, meaning aniline is a weaker base. In aniline, the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is in conjugation with the π electrons of the benzene ring. This delocalization reduces the electron density on nitrogen, making the lone pair less available for donation to a proton (H⁺). In methylamine, the –CH₃ group is electron-donating (by inductive effect), which increases the electron density on nitrogen, making the lone pair more readily available for proton acceptance. Therefore, methylamine is a stronger base (lower pKb) than aniline.

(i) Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic character in an aqueous solution: (CH₃)₃N, (CH₃)₂NH, NH₃, CH₃NH₂
OR
(ii) Why ammonolysis of alkyl halides is not a good method to prepare pure amines?

key_points: (i) NH₃ < CH₃NH₂ < (CH₃)₃N < (CH₃)₂NH (in aqueous solution, 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃)
(ii) Ammonolysis gives a mixture of primary, secondary, tertiary amines and quaternary ammonium salts — cannot get pure product

sub_questions.solution:
(i) In aqueous solution, the order of basicity is: NH₃ < CH₃NH₂ < (CH₃)₃N < (CH₃)₂NH. In the gas phase, basicity increases with alkyl substitution due to the inductive effect. However, in aqueous solution, solvation (hydration) of the cationic ammonium ion formed also plays a role. The conjugate acid of (CH₃)₂NH has two N–H bonds available for H-bonding with water (good solvation), making it the most basic in water. Trimethylamine (CH₃)₃N has no N–H bonds, so its conjugate acid is poorly solvated despite having three methyl groups. NH₃ has the lowest basicity due to no alkyl groups.

(ii) Ammonolysis of alkyl halides (R–X + NH₃) is not a good method to prepare pure amines because the reaction does not stop at the primary amine stage. The primary amine formed (R–NH₂) is more nucleophilic than NH₃ and reacts further with another molecule of alkyl halide to give secondary amine (R₂NH), then tertiary amine (R₃N), and finally a quaternary ammonium salt (R₄N⁺X⁻). The result is a mixture of all these products, which are difficult to separate, making it impractical for obtaining a pure amine.

(A) (a) Calculate the standard Gibbs energy (Δ_rG°) of the following reaction at 25°C: Au(s) + Ca²⁺(1M) → Au³⁺(1M) + Ca(s), E°Au³⁺/Au = +1.5 V, E°Ca²⁺/Ca = –2.87 V. Predict whether the reaction will be spontaneous or not at 25°C. [1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]  (b) Tarnished silver contains Ag₂S. Can this tarnish be removed by placing tarnished silverware in an aluminium pan containing an inert electrolytic solution such as NaCl? The standard electrode potential for half reaction: Ag₂S(s) + 2e⁻ → 2Ag(s) + S²⁻ is –0.71 V and for Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → 2Al(s) is –1.66 V.
OR
(B) (a) Define the following: (i) Cell potential  (ii) Fuel cell  (b) Calculate emf of the following cell at 25°C: Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(0.1M)||Cd²⁺(0.01M)|Cd(s). Given: E°Cd²⁺/Cd = –0.40 V, E°Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V, [log 10 = 1]

key_points: (A)(a) E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode; anode is Au/Au³⁺ (reversed), cathode is Ca²⁺/Ca; E°cell = –2.87 – 1.5 = –4.37 V; n=6; ΔrG° = –nFE°cell = –6×96500×(–4.37) = +2530410 J = +2530.41 kJ; positive ΔrG° means non-spontaneous
(A)(b) E°cell = –0.71 – (–1.66) = +0.95 V > 0; reaction is spontaneous; yes tarnish can be removed
(B)(a)(i) Cell potential: potential difference between two electrodes of a cell
(B)(a)(ii) Fuel cell: galvanic cell that converts chemical energy of a fuel directly to electrical energy

questions.solution:
(A)(a) The given cell reaction is: Au(s) + Ca²⁺(1M) → Au³⁺(1M) + Ca(s). Here, Au is oxidized (anode) and Ca²⁺ is reduced (cathode). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = E°(Ca²⁺/Ca) – E°(Au³⁺/Au) = (–2.87) – (+1.5) = –4.37 V. For the balanced reaction, Au → Au³⁺ loses 3e⁻ and Ca²⁺ → Ca gains 2e⁻; to balance electrons, n = LCM(3,2) = 6. ΔrG° = –nFE°cell = –6 × 96500 × (–4.37) = +2,530,410 J ≈ +2530.4 kJ mol⁻¹. Since ΔrG° is positive, the reaction is non-spontaneous under standard conditions at 25°C.

(A)(b) For the cell: Ag₂S reduced at cathode (E° = –0.71 V) and Al oxidized at anode (E° = –1.66 V for reduction, so oxidation potential = +1.66 V). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.71 – (–1.66) = +0.95 V. Since E°cell > 0, the reaction is spontaneous. Yes, the tarnish (Ag₂S) can be removed by placing tarnished silverware in an aluminium pan with NaCl solution. Aluminium acts as the anode and is oxidized, while Ag₂S is reduced back to Ag at the cathode.

(B)(a)(i) Cell potential (or EMF of the cell) is the potential difference between the two electrodes (cathode and anode) of an electrochemical cell when no current is flowing. It is a measure of the driving force of the cell reaction and is given by E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode.

(B)(a)(ii) A fuel cell is a galvanic (electrochemical) cell that converts the chemical energy of a fuel (such as hydrogen or methane) and an oxidant (oxygen from air) directly into electrical energy through electrochemical reactions without combustion. For example, in a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell: H₂ is oxidized at the anode and O₂ is reduced at the cathode, producing water as the only by-product.

(B)(b) The cell is: Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(0.1M)||Cd²⁺(0.01M)|Cd(s). Zn is anode (oxidized), Cd is cathode (reduced). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = E°(Cd²⁺/Cd) – E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = (–0.40) – (–0.76) = +0.36 V. Cell reaction: Zn + Cd²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cd; n = 2. Using Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0592/n) × log Q = 0.36 – (0.0592/2) × log([Zn²⁺]/[Cd²⁺]) = 0.36 – 0.0296 × log(0.1/0.01) = 0.36 – 0.0296 × log(10) = 0.36 – 0.0296 × 1 = 0.36 – 0.0296 = 0.3304 V.

questions.solution:
(A) Compound A has molecular formula C₂H₆O. It oxidizes with CrO₃ to give B; since C₂H₆O is ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH, a primary alcohol), oxidation with CrO₃ gives acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) as compound B. B on warming with I₂/NaOH(aq) gives a yellow precipitate — this is the iodoform test, and the yellow precipitate is CHI₃ (iodoform), so C = CHI₃. When A (ethanol) is heated with conc. H₂SO₄ at 413 K (intramolecular dehydration), compound D = CH₂=CH₂ (ethylene) is formed. D (ethylene/ethene) on reaction with excess HI gives E = CH₃CH₂I (ethyl iodide, iodoethane) by addition of HI.

Chemical equations:
1. CH₃CH₂OH + CrO₃ → CH₃CHO (A→B)
2. CH₃CHO + 3I₂ + 3NaOH → CHI₃↓ + CH₃COONa + 3NaI + 3H₂O (B→C, iodoform reaction)
3. CH₃CH₂OH (conc. H₂SO₄, 413K) → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (A→D, dehydration)
4. CH₂=CH₂ + 2HI (excess) → CH₃CH₂I (D→E, addition)

(B)(a)(i) Phenol reacts with concentrated HNO₃ (using conc. H₂SO₄ as catalyst) to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid):
C₆H₅OH + 3HNO₃ (conc. H₂SO₄) → 2,4,6-(NO₂)₃C₆H₂OH + 3H₂O

(B)(a)(ii) Hydroboration-oxidation of propene:
CH₃CH=CH₂ + B₂H₆ → (CH₃CH₂CH₂)₃B
(CH₃CH₂CH₂)₃B + H₂O₂/OH⁻ → 3CH₃CH₂CH₂OH (propan-1-ol)
The reaction follows anti-Markovnikov addition, giving propan-1-ol.

(B)(a)(iii) Williamson synthesis:
(CH₃)₃CONa + CH₃Cl → (CH₃)₃C–O–CH₃ + NaCl (methyl tert-butyl ether)

(B)(b) Lucas test can distinguish between butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol. Add Lucas reagent (anhydrous ZnCl₂ in conc. HCl) to each alcohol. Butan-2-ol (secondary alcohol) gives turbidity within 5 minutes due to formation of insoluble alkyl chloride. Butan-1-ol (primary alcohol) requires heating and shows turbidity only after a long time or not at room temperature.

(B)(c) Increasing order of acid strength: ethanol < water < phenol. Ethanol is the weakest acid because the alkyl group donates electrons, destabilizing the ethoxide anion. Water is stronger than ethanol because it has no electron-donating alkyl group. Phenol is the strongest because the phenoxide ion (C₆H₅O⁻) is stabilized by delocalization of the negative charge into the benzene ring through resonance.

questions.solution:
(A)(a) The compound CH₃–CH=CH–CHO has: a 4-carbon chain (but-), a double bond between C2 and C3 (2-en or but-2-en-), and an aldehyde group at C1 (–al). IUPAC name: But-2-enal.

(A)(b) To distinguish propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) from propanone (CH₃COCH₃): Tollens' test — add Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate). Propanal, being an aldehyde, reduces Ag⁺ to Ag and gives a silver mirror on the test tube wall. Propanone, being a ketone, does not reduce Tollens' reagent and gives no silver mirror. Alternatively, Fehling's test can be used: propanal gives a brick-red precipitate of Cu₂O, while propanone gives no precipitate.

(A)(c)(i) Toluene to benzoic acid: Toluene (C₆H₅CH₃) is oxidized by hot acidified KMnO₄ (or K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺). The methyl group is oxidized to –COOH: C₆H₅CH₃ + [O] (KMnO₄, H⁺, Δ) → C₆H₅COOH (benzoic acid).

(A)(c)(ii) Ethanol to propan-2-ol: Step 1: Oxidize ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ to give acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO). Step 2: Treat acetaldehyde with methylmagnesium bromide (CH₃MgBr, a Grignard reagent), followed by hydrolysis, to give propan-2-ol (CH₃CH(OH)CH₃): CH₃CHO + CH₃MgBr → CH₃CH(OMgBr)CH₃ → (H₃O⁺) CH₃CH(OH)CH₃.

(A)(c)(iii) Propanal to 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid): Step 1: Add HCN to propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) to give the cyanohydrin 2-hydroxypropanenitrile (CH₃CH(OH)CN) via nucleophilic addition. Step 2: Hydrolyse the –CN group with dilute acid (H⁺/H₂O) or base to give –COOH: CH₃CH(OH)CN + H₂O/H⁺ → CH₃CH(OH)COOH (2-hydroxypropanoic acid / lactic acid).

(B)(a) Cyclopentanone + HO–NH₂ (hydroxylamine) under H⁺ catalyst → Cyclopentanone oxime (the C=O becomes C=N–OH). This is a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction.

(B)(b) The starting material must be a compound that upon ozonolysis (O₃ followed by Zn/H₂O reductive workup) gives 2 molecules of cyclobutanone. This means the starting alkene must have a C=C double bond connecting two cyclobutyl rings: the starting material is bicyclobutylidene (1,1'-bi(cyclobutylidene)) or more precisely cyclobutylidenecyclobutane — two cyclobutane rings joined by a C=C double bond.

(B)(c) Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid + SOCl₂ (Δ) → Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarbonyl dichloride (if both –COOH groups react separately, forming the diacid chloride). Alternatively, due to proximity of the two –COOH groups (cis isomer), intramolecular cyclization with SOCl₂ could give the cyclic anhydride (cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic anhydride). The most likely product under SOCl₂/Δ is the cyclic anhydride.

(B)(d) 2-formylcyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid (cyclohexane ring with –CHO and –COOH groups) + NaCN/HCl → NaCN adds to the aldehyde (–CHO) via nucleophilic addition to give a cyanohydrin: the –CHO becomes –CH(OH)CN. The –COOH group remains unaffected under these conditions. Product: 2-(1-hydroxycyanomethyl)cyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid.

(B)(e) Benzene → Acetophenone (phenyl methyl ketone, C₆H₅COCH₃): This is achieved by Friedel-Crafts acylation. Benzene is treated with acetyl chloride (CH₃COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ (Lewis acid catalyst): C₆H₆ + CH₃COCl (AlCl₃) → C₆H₅COCH₃ + HCl.
